analysis.investment_thesis: Rikhav Securities ticks several SMILE boxes — 159 Cr market cap, 64% promoter holding, P/E of 6.6, and revenue 9x'd from 36 Cr to 328 Cr in three years. However, stockbroking is a cyclical, commoditized business and FY25 net profit already fell 43% (42→24 Cr) despite revenue tripling, signaling the bull-market tailwind is masking structural margin pressure.
key_strengths: Sweet-spot small cap (159 Cr) with 64% promoter holding and cheap 6.63 P/E
Revenue CAGR 108.9% (36→328 Cr); debt slashed to just 5 Cr in FY25
30-year vintage (since 1995) — management has seen multiple cycles
key_risks: Profit declining in FY25 despite revenue surge — operating income down 55→34 Cr signals margin compression
Stockbroking is highly cyclical; bear market will crush earnings quickly
OCF deeply negative (-188 Cr FY25); only 1/4 years of positive operating cash flow
red_flags: Net profit and operating income both contracted in FY25 even as revenue 3x'd
Reserves jumped 124→225 Cr suggesting recent equity raise/IPO dilution
Other income collapsed to 0 — prior profits were flattered by non-core items
analysis.detailed_analysis: From a SMILE lens, Rikhav is Small (159 Cr — excellent), has Medium-to-long experience (since 1995), promoter holding is strong at 64%, and valuation at 6.6x P/E is attractive. But the 'Large aspiration' and 'Extra-large TAM with underpenetration' boxes don't convincingly tick — stockbroking in India is crowded (Zerodha, Groww, Angel One, ICICI Direct) and Rikhav is a sub-scale regional player with no obvious niche or transformation catalyst. The explosive topline is almost entirely a reflection of the FY24-25 retail bull market rather than a structural moat.\n\nThe numbers that worry me: operating income peaked at 55 Cr in FY24 and fell to 34 Cr in FY25 despite revenue going from 111 to 328 Cr — that's a massive margin collapse (49% → 10%). Net profit fell 42→24 Cr in the same window. This is not a compounding story; it's a cyclical broker enjoying volumes but losing pricing power. Add deeply volatile cash flows (OCF -188 Cr in FY25) and what looks like a recent equity raise, and the cheap P/E becomes a value trap risk if markets turn. I'd watch FY26 Q1-Q2 numbers before committing — if margins stabilize and they show a genuine product pivot (AMC, wealth, fintech), revisit. Otherwise pass.
